speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are pregnant and experiencing fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. To help me determine the cause, have you noticed any rash, muscle pain, or difficulty breathing?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count
REQUEST TEST: C-Reactive_Protein

speaker: Doctor
text:
The Complete Blood Count and C-Reactive Protein results are normal. Given your pregnancy, fever, headache, and systemic symptoms, could you describe any specific type of headache (e.g., severe, frontal) or report any visual disturbances or sudden swelling in your face or hands?

REQUEST TEST: Urine_Microscopy_and_Culture
REQUEST TEST: Serology_Lyme

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the normal laboratory results. Since standard bacterial markers and initial serology are negative, could you tell me if you have recently consumed unpasteurized cheese, raw meat, or if you have been spending time around pets or outdoor animals?

REQUEST TEST: Toxoplasma_IgG_IgM
REQUEST TEST: Rubella_IgM
REQUEST IMAGES: Fundoscopy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Toxoplasma_IgG: Positive, Toxoplasma_IgM: Negative, Rubella_IgM: Negative, Fundoscopy: Normal retinal appearance with no chorioretinitis lesions.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Toxoplasmosis (Acute maternal infection).

The positive Toxoplasma IgG indicates prior exposure or recent infection, and since IgM is negative, this likely represents a chronic or past infection rather than an acute primary infection in pregnancy. However, given your symptoms, I need to clarify: do you recall any past diagnosis of toxoplasmosis, or is it possible you have been exposed recently despite the negative IgM? Also, have you noticed any swollen lymph nodes?
